chapter_title: Concerning the Wheel and the Conduits
chapter_note: The chapter is largely a compact core teaching explaining a cosmological mechanic (wheel vs. pneumatic conduits) through analogies (ship in water; bird in air). Paragraph 1 is a dialogue/question frame. Paragraph 2 contains a frame attribution at its head (“The enlightener says to them:”) but the remainder is impersonal mechanical teaching; thus MIXED with the attribution removed. No pastoral drift, no NT overlay, no institutional seam extensions.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Direct disciple address and petition formula (“His disciples say to him… Convince us, our master…”) functions as dialogue apparatus introducing the topic, not the teaching layer.

paragraphs.core_text: The reason that the conduits shall not be cut, for they are not cut, is because they are spiritual. Thus the conduits are like the waters through which ships sail. You shall find the prow that is in position in the front part of the ship divides the waters, casting them back and forth. So, when it parts the waters and that ship opens up the water with its cleaving prow, immediately and without delay the waters mingle with each other again behind the ship; and the path of the ship shall not be discernible in the midst of the waters.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue attribution/frame formula: “The enlightener says to them:” (layered hagiographic/compilation voice marker).
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core mechanic explanation (pneumatic conduits not severed) with a natural-process analogy; no citation, no institutional instruction. Only the initial speaker tag is later framing.

paragraphs.core_text: Just as when a bird flies up in the air, for its path is not visible in the air, and in the way of mankind, in the sun within the conduits. They also shall not be tangled up in them, and neither shall you find their path through the air known.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Impersonal analogical extension of the same physical/cosmological principle (path not visible; no entanglement). No dialogue apparatus or ecclesial/NT material.

paragraphs.core_text: This is also the case with the wheel. It turns through the conduits and the air. The wheel shall not cut the conduits, nor are the conduits themselves entangled in the wheel.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Concise closure stating the cosmological conclusion in explanatory voice; no framing, citation, or pastoral application.
